questions.q: Why is the resource group the first thing Theo creates, before the storage account or the VM?
options: Because Azure requires resource groups to be created at a specific time of day
Because everything in this project shares one lifecycle, and the resource group is the container that holds that lifecycle together
Because storage accounts cannot be created without an existing VM
Because tags can only be applied after a VM already exists
questions.explain: A resource group is the logical container for resources that are created, managed, and eventually retired together -- exactly what this project's resources need.

questions.q: Why does `az storage account create` use `Standard_LRS` and `StorageV2` for the product images?
options: Standard_LRS and StorageV2 are the only options Azure offers
Premium tier is required for any blob storage account
Standard tier fits data that doesn't need sub-millisecond latency, and StorageV2 is the general-purpose kind that supports blob storage along with everything else the account might need
StorageV2 is required specifically for product images and no other file type
questions.explain: Product images don't need Premium-tier latency, and StorageV2 is the modern general-purpose default used in nearly every real deployment.

questions.q: What does a single `az vm create` command actually provision, beyond "just a VM"?
options: Only the virtual machine itself, with nothing else
The VM, an OS disk, a network interface, and, by default, a public IP address and a network security group
The VM and a pre-installed copy of the catalog application
A full backup of the on-prem server
questions.explain: One `az vm create` command provisions a small bundle of resources, not just the VM -- the OS disk, NIC, and (unless told otherwise) a public IP and NSG.

questions.q: Why was `Standard_B2s` chosen as the VM size for vm-catalog01?
options: It's the only size Azure allows for a first project
It's a burstable size that fits a catalog app with steady-but-not-huge traffic today, with room to upsize later if monitoring shows it's needed
It's the most expensive size, which guarantees reliability
D-series VMs cannot run Ubuntu
questions.explain: B-series fits unpredictable, moderate load without over-provisioning; if real monitoring data later shows a need for sustained CPU, upsizing to D-series is a simple follow-up, not a reason to guess bigger now.

questions.q: What does `az resource list --resource-group rg-driftwood-eastus-catalog` show that `az vm list` would not?
options: Nothing different -- they return identical results
Only resources created before today
Every resource actually in the group regardless of type -- the VM plus its disk, NIC, public IP, and default VNet, not just VMs
Only resources with a specific tag
questions.explain: `az resource list` returns everything in a resource group regardless of type, which is the honest way to confirm what a command like `az vm create` actually created as side effects.
